questiontext.text:
The variables \(x\) and \(y\) are related by the power law \[ y = k\,x^{n}, \] where \(k\) and \(n\) are constants. The experimental data are:

\(x\)\(y\)
\({@x1@}\)\({@y1@}\)
\({@x2@}\)\({@y2@}\)
\({@x3@}\)\({@y3@}\)

By plotting a suitable straight-line graph, determine the constants. Give values to 2 decimal places where appropriate.

\( n = \) [[input:ansn]] [[validation:ansn]] [[feedback:prtn]]
\( k = \) [[input:ansk]] [[validation:ansk]] [[feedback:prtk]]

generalfeedback.text:
Solution.

  1. Linearise. Take logarithms (base 10) of \(y=k\,x^{n}\): \[ \log_{10} y = n\,\log_{10} x + \log_{10} k, \] so a graph of \(Y=\log_{10} y\) against \(X=\log_{10} x\) is a straight line with gradient \(m=n\) and intercept \(c=\log_{10} k\).
  2. Find the gradient \(n\). Using the first and last transformed points, \[ n=\frac{Y_3-Y_1}{X_3-X_1}=\frac{{@dispdp(py3,2)@}-{@dispdp(py1,2)@}}{{@dispdp(px3,2)@}-{@dispdp(px1,2)@}}={@nval@}. \]
  3. Find the intercept. Substitute the point \(({@dispdp(px1,2)@},\,{@dispdp(py1,2)@})\) into \(Y=nX+c\): \[ {@dispdp(py1,2)@}={@nval@}\times{@dispdp(px1,2)@}+c \;\Rightarrow\; c={@dispdp(cval,2)@}=\log_{10} k \;\Rightarrow\; k=10^{{@dispdp(cval,2)@}}={@kval@}. \]
  4. State the values: \(n={@nval@}\) and \(k={@kval@}\).

The graph of \(\log_{10} y\) against \(\log_{10} x\), with the gradient triangle and the intercept, is shown below.

falsefeedback.text: \(n\) is the gradient of \(\log_{10} y\) against \(\log_{10} x\).
